strengths: Significance: Clustering weakly connected directed graphs without teleportation is a useful problem. Combining vertex reweighting with diffusion offers a flexible approach to exploring cluster structure at different scales.

Soundness: For a valid transition matrix and strictly positive vertex measure, Eq. (4) constructs a reversible stochastic operator with stationary weights proportional to ν+ξ. This provides a sound starting point for the proposed framework.

Empirical promise: Experiments cover 11 UCI datasets and four networks. Importantly, Appendix Tables 4 and 6 include label-free CH/DCH parameter selection for a simplified variant: its average UCI NMI is 63.45 versus 60.01 for PIC, and its Cora NMI is 49.71 versus 30.65 for RSC. These results provide evidence beyond the ground-truth-tuned main tables.

Presentation and ethics: The high-level workflow is understandable, with pseudocode, parameter grids, dataset dimensions, and supplementary experiments. Benchmark sources and funding are identified; no material research-ethics concern is evident. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b08/review-experiment-_ymzmnoj/call-45cd7ab4d8f646bbad5b80d0c2f1d64a/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: Central soundness issue: Eqs. (6)–(7) are inconsistent. The diffusion-distance Gram matrix is P_ν^t D_{π_ν}^{-1}(P_ν^t)^T = P_ν^{2t}D_{π_ν}^{-1}, whereas Eq. (7) uses P_ν^tD_{ν+ξ}^{-1}. This is more than a normalization discrepancy: for an unweighted triangle with ν=1 and t=1, the claimed quadratic form is -1/2, while the squared diffusion distance is 3/2. Moreover, Algorithm 1 applies ordinary k-means to kernel rows, inducing KK^T geometry rather than K. Correcting the exponent alone therefore would not establish the claimed connection between the diffusion distance and the implemented embedding.

Applicability assumptions are incomplete. Self-adjointness and aperiodicity do not establish irreducibility; Eq. (4) cannot connect distinct weak components. The inverses involving out-degree, in-degree, and ν also require explicit treatment of sinks, sources, and zero measures. Consequently, the claims of applicability to arbitrary digraphs 'without any restriction' are unsupported.

Evaluation does not establish the full method's unsupervised superiority. Section 6.1 selects parameters against ground truth and reports best-of-100 restarts, without a held-out protocol or uncertainty estimates. The proposed method's substantially larger search space further complicates comparison. The appendix's label-free experiments partially address this concern but use a reduced variant. Additionally, Algorithm 2 selects diffusion time using ν=1 and unnormalized walk embeddings; no convincing analysis establishes that this time transfers to the final parametrized kernel.

Originality and attribution of improvements remain insufficiently established. Eq. (4) is directly I minus the generalized random-walk Laplacian already credited to Sevi et al. (2022), while the Gram-matrix interpretation follows standard diffusion geometry. The combination could be useful, but comparisons against that prior generalized spectral clustering method and alternative embeddings of the same operator are missing. Directionality claims also need controlled evidence: with α=0, Appendix Eq. (12) reduces to a walk on W+W^T, including the best Cora configuration in Table 2.

Reproducibility is weakened by inconsistent specifications. Section 6.1 gives an integer RSC parameter grid from 1 to 20, but Table 2 reports values such as 0.2 and 2.5. Appendix Eq. (12) changes the stationary weights to ν̃+ξ without clearly specifying the corresponding update to the kernel normalization. No implementation link, random seeds, or sufficient clarification of restart selection is supplied. These ambiguities make it difficult to determine precisely which algorithm produced the results.

Significance and limitations: Scalability and computational efficiency are not demonstrated. The largest evaluated graph has 2,485 vertices, only two network benchmarks are directed, and no runtime or memory measurements are reported. Matrix powers generally become dense, while Algorithm 1 uses N-dimensional embeddings. The practical cost of these operations and the extensive parameter search needs characterization, alongside sensitivity and failure-case analysis.
